The regulations issued by Commodity 
Credit Corporation and the Production
and Marketing Administration published 
in 18 F. R. 2733, and containing the 
specific requirements for the 1953-Crop 
Wheat Price Support Program are here­
by amended as follows:
Section 601.110 (a) is amended by de­
leting from subparagraph (2) the words 
“except as provided in subparagraph (3) 
of this paragraph;” by adding a proviso 
at the end of subparagraph (2); by de­
leting all of subparagraph (3); and by 
changing the designation of subpara­
graph (4) to subparagraph (3), so that 
the amended paragraph reads as follows:
§601.110 S e ttle m e n t— (a) Farm- 
storage loans. (1) In the case of eligible 
wheat delivered to CCC from farm stor­
age under the loan program, settlement 
shall be made at the applicable support 
rate for the approved point of delivery. 
The support rate shall be for the grade 
and quality of the total quantity of wheat 
eligible for delivery.
(2) If, upon delivery, the wheat under 
farm-storage loan is of a grade and/or 
quality for which no support rate has 
been established, the settlement value 
shall be computed at the support rate es­
tablished for the grade and/or quality 
of the wheat placed under loan less the 
difference, if any, at the time of delivery, 
between the market price for the grade 
and/or quality placed under loan and 
the market price of the wheat delivered, 
as determined by CCC: Provided, how­
ever, That if such wheat is sold by CCC 
in order to determine its market price 
the settlement value shall not be less 
than such sales price.
(3) If farm-stored wheat is delivered 
to CCC prior to April 30, 1954, upon re­
quest of the producer and with the ap­
proval of CCC, the loan settlement shall 
be reduced as set forth in §  601.109.
(Sec. 4, 62 Stat. 1070, as amended; 15 U. S. C.  
Sup. 714b. Interprets or applies sec. 5, 62  
Stat. 1072, secs. 101, 401, 63 Stat. 1051, 1054;  
15 U. S. C. Sup. 714c, 7 U. S. C. Sup. 1441,  
1421)

research_rationale:
EO 10468 (signed 1953-07-07 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1953-07-07, 4:09 p.m.; 18 FR 3979, Federal Register of July 9, 1953 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10468.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative paragraph and one closing sentence. The paragraph appoints William C. Strand, Director, Office of Territories, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice James P. Davis, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise and discharge the functions, duties and authority that Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 conferred on the Administration and its Administrator. The closing sentence amends those orders accordingly. There is no deadline, sunset or condition. First end: both commands are one-time acts. The appointment was made, and the amendments to the earlier orders took effect, when the order was signed; the text has no effective-date wording, so the signing date 1953-07-07 is recorded (the filing date is the same day). What survives is a consequence of the performed appointment and not a continuing command of this order: Strand's holding of the office and the earlier orders as amended. The functions he exercises come from Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689, not from this order. No held source shows when Strand left the office or when the Administration ended. A contents line in the held Federal Register text printed with EO 10597 (issue of 1955-02-17) lists an Interior Department notice on cessation of functions and activities of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration at 20 FR 1027; the notice itself is not held. Those facts concern the surviving appointment and the earlier orders, not whether this order's own commands were performed. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10468 found only the order's own copies and a page number in another document; a scan of held order texts numbered above 10468 for the Administration's name and for Strand's name found no order. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search, which found no hit for the appointee.

EO 10512 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10512.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: two recitals, which command nothing (that Executive Order 9047 exempted certain officers and employees from automatic separation for an indefinite period, and that the public interest no longer requires the exemption), one operative command revoking Executive Order 9047 under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and one effective-date sentence making the order effective at the close of business on March 31, 1954. First end: the revocation is a one-time act with a fixed effective moment, so it was performed, and the clause spent, at the close of business on March 31, 1954. Nothing in the held texts postpones or changes that moment. The consequence, that Executive Order 9047 no longer exempts anyone, is a completed result and not a command that continues. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10512 found only the order's own copies, the next two orders printed in the same issue (EO 10513 and 10514) and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Inventory: one operative paragraph. Under section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue Code it orders that any return on Form 990-A made by an organization exempt under section 101(6) of the Code, for the years 1950 to 1953 inclusive, be open to inspection until and including January 3, 1955 by the special committee of the House of Representatives authorized by House Resolution 217, 83d Congress, agreed to July 27, 1953, to investigate tax-exempt foundations, for carrying out that resolution and subject to the Treasury decision on inspection of returns by committees of Congress approved the same day; the order takes effect on filing for publication. research_rationale:
EO 10523 (signed 1954-03-26 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-03-29, 10:13 a.m.; 19 FR 1689, Federal Register of March 30, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10523.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: four recitals (the Goethals memorial authorized by Congress, the Commission's report that its work is complete, the anniversaries, and the wish to dedicate the memorial), which command nothing, and two numbered commands. Item 1 designates Wednesday, March 31, 1954 as the day for dedicating the memorial to Major General George W. Goethals in the Canal Zone and allows the Governor of the Canal Zone to arrange ceremonies. Item 2 excuses federal officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama from duty on March 31, 1954, with the usual exceptions, and treats the day as a holiday on the Isthmus within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. First end: both items are limited to the single day March 31, 1954, so each was performed and spent at the close of that day. The text has no until-wording and no extension or renewal. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8), so it cannot end this order; the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10523 found only the order's own copy, the preceding order's text that prints the same issue contents, and unrelated page numbers. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

EO 10569 (signed 1954-10-05 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-10-07, 10:12 a.m.; 19 FR 6493, Federal Register of October 8, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10569.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier inventory lists eleven clauses, but ten of them are Civil Service Commission notices printed after the order on the same Federal Register page (subsections (k), (b) and (e) of the exceptions from the competitive service) and are not part of this order. I replace the inventory with one clause, characters 1180 to 1563 of the registered file: the sentence that amends Executive Order 10334 of March 26, 1952, which exempted Frederick C. Mayer, organist and choirmaster at the United States Military Academy, from compulsory retirement for an indefinite period, by substituting the words until December 31, 1954 for the words for an indefinite period of time in its last paragraph, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932. The two recitals command nothing. First end: the amended exemption runs until December 31, 1954. Following the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates, the end is recorded as that stated date, inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 31, 1954); the exclusive reading is the alternative, under which the exemption ends when December 31, 1954 begins. The amending act itself was performed when the order took effect; the lifecycle of this order is the period it fixed for the exemption. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10569 found only the order's own copies and unrelated page numbers; a scan for the appointee's name found Executive Order 10334, the recitals of this order, and no later order extending or renewing the exemption; the person-name machine search found no hit. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search.

research_rationale:
EO 10580 (signed 1954-12-04 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-12-06, 11:32 a.m.; 19 FR 8037, Federal Register of December 7, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10580.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative sentence with two joined commands limited to two days. First, the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, are closed all day on Friday, December 24, 1954 and one-half day on Friday, December 31, 1954. Second, federal employees in that area and in the field service, except those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law, are excused from duty on that day and that half day, each of which is a holiday within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. There is no recital, report deadline, extension or renewal. First end: by its own terms the order operates only on those two days, so it was fully performed at the close of December 31, 1954; the December 24 closing was spent earlier. The text has no until-wording, so the end is the last stated day. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8); it cannot end this order, and the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10580 found no order text that names it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

By virtue of thé authority vested in me  
as President of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered that the several executive  
departments, independent establish­
ments, and other governmental agencies  
in the metropolitan area of the District  
of Columbia, including the General Ac­
counting Office, the Government Print­
ing Office, and the Navy Yard and Naval  
Stations, shall be closed all day on Fri­
day, December 24, 1954, the day pre­
ceding Christmas Day, and one-half day  
on Friday, December 31, 1954, the day  
preceding New Year’s Day; and all em­
ployees in the Federal service in the  
metropolitan area of the District of  
Columbia, and in the field service of the  
executive departments, independent  
establishments, and other agencies of  
the Government, except those who may  
for special public reasons be excluded  
from the provisions of this order by the  
heads of their respective departments,  
establishments, or agencies, or those  
whose absence from duty would be in­
consistent with the provisions of exist­
ing law, shall be excused from duty on  
such day and such one-half day; and  
such day and one-half day shall each be  
considered a holiday within the meaning  
of Executive Order No. 10358 of June 9,  
1952, and of all statutes so far as they  
relate to the compensation and leave of  
employees of the United States.
